A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices. Content can be matched across the appendix reorganization and figure combinations.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and the supplementary figures report original R1-32B and s1-32B experiments on 30 AIME 2024 questions, including accuracy, confidence, and utility results.

after.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A–B report original experiments on 60 AIME 2024/2025 questions and 198 GPQA Diamond questions.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same reasoning-budget enforcement, answer-token confidence calculation, and threshold-based abstention procedure. The additional evaluations do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluation on GPQA Diamond, extending coverage from competition mathematics to graduate-level multiple-choice physics, biology, and chemistry. This substantially broadens the domains and answer requirements tested.

E2.justification: R1-32B and s1/S1-32B remain the evaluated model pair, with the same threshold-zero comparisons. GPQA uses this same pair; newly cited calibration and budget-control methods are not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: The AIME evaluation expands from 30 questions from 2024 to 60 from 2024–2025. The added GPQA protocol uses 198 questions and budgets of 500–4,000 tokens. The retained AIME budget range, 100-token increments, confidence thresholds, and payoff settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 3 adds confidence trajectories for 10 randomly selected questions, providing limited case-level evidence about confidence evolution. The aggregate R1/S1 confidence analyses already appeared in v1 Figures 3 and 7; combining those plots alone is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both show fitted confidence trends; the newly specified cubic fit and illustrative question selection do not establish changed uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: AIME curves change with the expanded question pool: at 8,000 tokens and threshold zero, R1 trails S1 in v1 Figure 2 but leads in v2 Figure 2. v2 Figures 8–10 add GPQA results showing a larger R1 advantage at high confidence thresholds. v2 also introduces unexplained scale discrepancies between utility surfaces and their stated slices in Figures 4–5 and 9–10.

T1.justification: Section 4 replaces the indicator-sum utility expression with an equivalent piecewise expression. Correct-answer, abstention, and incorrect-answer payoffs remain unchanged, as do the three risk settings. No substantive theorem, assumption, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims about compute improving confidence, selective answering revealing performance differences, and reporting Jeopardy Odds alongside conventional evaluation.

C2.justification: The new GPQA discussion attributes similar low-threshold behavior to its four-choice format. The Limitations section adds possible harm from budget-forcing truncation and distribution mismatch, while removing v1's explicit caveat about testing only three utility settings.

D1.justification: v2 reports a code-release URL and specifies 32-bit precision and cubic trend fitting, but removes the approximately four-hour runtime estimate. Existing library and four-H100 hardware information moves from Appendix A.2 into Section 3.1.

R1.justification: v2 updates positioning against concurrent confidence and self-verification work, adds budget-control and GPQA references, and removes the earlier tool-use and human-calibration discussion. Much of the longer main-text related work is relocated from v1 Appendix A.1.

P1.justification: Existing implementation and background material moves into Sections 3.1 and 5, with numbered subsections, acknowledgments, and local wording edits. The abstract, introduction, methods, conclusion, and overall narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 combines the separate R1/S1 confidence plots into a full-width Figure 3 with trajectory overlays, combines the S1 accuracy and utility surfaces into Figure 6, redraws and relocates plots, and adds GPQA Figures 8–10. This substantially revises the visual presentation of the evidence.

improvement.justification: The expanded AIME evaluation, GPQA experiments, and code-release information strengthen evidence and reproducibility documentation. However, v2 introduces unexplained inconsistencies in its central utility results: Figure 5 reaches approximately -2 where the corresponding Figure 4 surface reaches -1, and GPQA Figures 9–10 also disagree in scale. The PDFs do not establish whether these are display rescalings or calculation problems, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
